userStories.title: Audit entries carry resolved names
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enrich GET /api/audit records with one batched, historical display-name projection without changing existing audit fields or pagination.

**Motivation** — The web cannot turn them into names for an auditor: the user, agent and runner list routes need other keys (`user.read`, `agent.read`, `fleet.runner.read`), and the project list shows only the caller's projects.

**Approach** — `AuditEntryDto` gains a `display` block, filled by `AuditLogService.list` after the page is read:

```ts
export interface AuditDisplay {
  actor: string | null;       // USER: name, else email; AGENT: Agent.name; RUNNER: Runner.name; SYSTEM: null
  onBehalfOf: string | null;  // USER: name, else email; AGENT: Agent.name; null when there is no onBehalfOf
  approver: string | null;    // USER: name, else email; AGENT: Agent.name; null when there is no approver
  project: { slug: string; name: string } | null;  // null when projectId is null
}
```

- A principal or project that no longer exists (or never existed: ids are not foreign keys) resolves to `null`. A soft-deleted project still resolves (the audit log is history).
- A `USER` whose `name` is null or blank resolves to the email.
- `SYSTEM` actors are never looked up: their `actor.id` is the component id (`scheduler`, `outbox`, `budget`, ...) and the web shows it as is.
- Resolution is one batch per page: `AuditLogService.list` collects the distinct ids per kind across the page's records (actor, onBehalfOf, approver, projectId) and calls `PrismaAuditEntryRepository.findDisplayNames` **once**. An empty page, or a page whose four id lists are all empty (for example only `SYSTEM` actors with no project), does not call it. `findDisplayNames` issues at most one `findMany` per non-empty id list (users, agents, runners, projects), selecting only the label fields.
- `AuditEntryDto.from(record, display?)`: `display` defaults to the all-null block, so existing callers keep their behaviour. `AuditLogService.list` maps with a closure (`(r) => AuditEntryDto.from(r, displayFor(r))`), never by passing `AuditEntryDto.from` itself to `remapPage` (which would pass the array index as `display`).
- `AuditDisplay`, `EMPTY_AUDIT_DISPLAY` (all four fields `null`) and `AuditDisplayNames` live in `apps/api/src/audit/domain/audit-entry.domain.ts`. `AuditDisplayNames` is `{ users: Map<string, string>; agents: Map<string, string>; runners: Map<string, string>; projects: Map<string, { slug: string; name: string }> }`, keyed by id.
- **Designer's call — cross-module label reads.** `.nax/rules/api-data.md` § Layering says a module reads another module's data through that module's service. `findDisplayNames` instead reads the label columns of `User`, `Agent`, `Runner` and `Project` from the audit repository, because the owning modules do not export a by-ids label lookup (`UsersModule` exports nothing), and wiring four domain modules into the global `AuditLogModule` couples it to all of them for a label projection. The read is a read-only label projection (`id` plus the label columns, `select` only), one `findMany` per kind, and never writes.

**Scope** — In: domain display types/constants, DTO display property/default, repository label projection, service enrichment, and unit/real-route integration tests. Preserve existing AC-1..AC-7 in audit-log.service.spec.ts and AC-8..AC-13 in dto/audit-entry.dto.spec.ts unchanged; extend setup() with findDisplayNames resolving four empty Maps. `findPage` is unchanged. Out: correlationId filtering and keys endpoint/spec generation (US-002), web models/composable/page (US-003 onward), and all audit write-path changes.

**Interface** — Target declarations:
```ts
@ApiProperty({ type: Object }) declare display: AuditDisplay;
static from(r: AuditEntryRecord, display: AuditDisplay = EMPTY_AUDIT_DISPLAY): AuditEntryDto
findDisplayNames(ids: { userIds: string[]; agentIds: string[]; runnerIds: string[]; projectIds: string[] }): Promise<AuditDisplayNames>
```

Testing: integration ACs boot the app like audit-route.integration.spec.ts (`bootHttpApp`, `seedFleetHttpWorld`, `fixtureDb(app)`) and call GET /api/audit with the root user's token. Insert entries directly with db.auditEntry.create. Use existing world.ids users updated with db.user.update (no new users), seedFleetHttpAgent for agents, insertRunner(db, { name }) for runners, and deletedAt on seeded ops for a soft-deleted project. Unit tests directly instantiate the service and repository with fakes; DB suites use the shared environment gate and must run outside the sandbox before merge. A rejected name lookup rejects the whole page with the original error, never a partially enriched result.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] When GET /api/audit returns an entry whose actor is a USER named Ada, display.actor equals 'Ada'.
[integration] When GET /api/audit returns an entry whose USER actor has name null, display.actor equals that user's email.
[integration] When GET /api/audit returns an entry whose USER actor has name '   ', display.actor equals that user's email.
[integration] When GET /api/audit returns an entry whose actor is an AGENT, display.actor equals that agent's name.
[integration] When GET /api/audit returns an entry whose RUNNER actor was created with name 'wk-mac', display.actor equals 'wk-mac'.
[integration] When GET /api/audit returns an entry whose actor is SYSTEM with id 'scheduler', display.actor is null.
[integration] When GET /api/audit returns an entry with onBehalfOfType USER and onBehalfOfId identifying a user named Bea, display.onBehalfOf equals 'Bea'.
[integration] When GET /api/audit returns an entry with approverType AGENT and approverId identifying an agent, display.approver equals that agent's name.
[integration] When GET /api/audit returns an entry whose projectId is the soft-deleted ops project, display.project equals { slug: 'ops', name: <the ops project's name> }.

[integration] When GET /api/audit returns an entry whose USER actor id, onBehalfOfId, approverId and projectId are all 'ghost' (matching no row), display equals { actor: null, onBehalfOf: null, approver: null, project: null } and the request succeeds.

[unit] When AuditLogService.list reads three records whose actors are the same USER 'u1' and whose projectIds are 'p1', 'p1' and 'p2', it records exactly one findDisplayNames call with { userIds: ['u1'], agentIds: [], runnerIds: [], projectIds: ['p1', 'p2'] }.
[unit] When AuditLogService.list reads an empty page, it does not call findDisplayNames.
[unit] When findDisplayNames rejects with an error, AuditLogService.list rejects with that same error.

[unit] When PrismaAuditEntryRepository.findDisplayNames({ userIds: ['u1'], agentIds: [], runnerIds: [], projectIds: [] }) runs over a fake Prisma client, it makes no findMany call other than user.findMany.
[unit] When AuditEntryDto.from(record) is called without a display, display equals { actor: null, onBehalfOf: null, approver: null, project: null }.

routing.reasoning: Four existing files in one audit module gain bounded label queries, maps and an optional DTO argument; no module wiring or authorization changes are needed, so ordinary TDD is sufficient.

`AuditEntryDto` gains `display` and `from` takes an optional display defaulting to `EMPTY_AUDIT_DISPLAY`.

userStories.title: Correlation filter and GET /api/audit/keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add exact correlationId filtering and a guarded distinct-key endpoint, then export the complete additive audit API contract.

**Motivation** — The key filter needs the set of keys that occur. The permission catalog does not cover it (audit keys include `runner.sync`, `thread.*` and `system.*` keys that are not catalog entries), so the API lists the distinct keys present.

**Approach** — API: correlation filter (US-002)

`ListAuditQuery` and the filter chain gain `correlationId` (`@IsOptional() @IsString() @MaxLength(128)`, exact match), passed through `AuditLogService.list` and `PrismaAuditEntryRepository.findPage` like the other id filters. It lets the page show every write of one request or run.

API: `GET /api/audit/keys` (US-002)

- `test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts` gains the route (200 with the admin token, 401 without credentials), as `.nax/rules/api-testing.md` requires for endpoint changes.
- `AuditController.keys()`, `@Get('keys')`, `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)`, `@Requires('audit.read')`, returns `JsonResponse.Ok({ keys })`.
- `keys` is the distinct `AuditEntry.key` values, sorted ascending (`PrismaAuditEntryRepository.findDistinctKeys()`: `findMany({ distinct: ['key'], select: { key: true }, orderBy: { key: 'asc' } })`), exposed through `AuditLogService.keys()`. The key set is small (catalog keys plus system and runner keys), so there is no paging.
- `openapi.json` is regenerated with `bun run api:export-spec` from the repo root, in US-002, after both contract changes exist; it gains the `GET /api/audit/keys` operation and the `correlationId` query parameter on `GET /api/audit`.

**Scope** — In: correlationId on ListAuditQuery/AuditListQuery/AuditEntryFilters and exact repository where clause, service.keys/repository.findDistinctKeys/controller.keys, integration/e2e/spec-integrity endpoint entries, service tests and root openapi.json regeneration. Existing assertions and decorator checks are unchanged. Out: display enrichment implementation (US-001), web API/query/page work (US-003 onward). A CLI `koda audit` command and regenerating `apps/cli/src/generated/` are out of scope. An `AuditEntryDto` or `AuditKeysDto` component schema in `openapi.json` is out of scope (the routes' `@ApiResponse` carries no `type`, as on `AuditController.list`).

**Interface** — Target declarations and query shape:
```ts
@IsOptional() @IsString() @MaxLength(128)
correlationId?: string
keys(): Promise<string[]>
findDistinctKeys(): Promise<string[]>
findMany({ distinct: ['key'], select: { key: true }, orderBy: { key: 'asc' } })
```

Keep audit.read global. GET /api/audit and /keys retain RequiresGuard enforcement regardless of project input; missing credentials give 401 and callers lacking audit.read give 403. Keep name enrichment from US-001 and existing newest-first ordering/UTC validation untouched. Add @ApiPropertyOptional for correlationId as on adjacent fields so export includes it. Add { path: '/api/audit/keys', method: 'get' } to test/integration/openapi-spec/spec-integrity.integration.spec.ts; add the authenticated and unauthenticated endpoint cases beside the existing audit block. Use the audit-route.integration.spec.ts HTTP app/fixture pattern and clear audit fixtures per case so distinct-key results are exact. Extend audit-log.service.spec.ts for correlation pass-through and keys() while keeping prior assertions unchanged. Run DB-backed specs outside the sandbox under the shared gate; preserve DB-free unit tests. Run only api:export-spec at the repository root after implementation, not generate:cli.

[integration] Given entries keyed 'comment.create', 'ticket.create' and 'comment.create', GET /api/audit/keys as the root user returns 200 with data.keys equal to ['comment.create', 'ticket.create'].
[integration] Given no audit entries, GET /api/audit/keys as the root user returns 200 with data.keys equal to [].

[integration] In endpoint.e2e.spec.ts, GET /api/audit/keys with the admin token returns 200.
[integration] In endpoint.e2e.spec.ts, GET /api/audit/keys without credentials returns 401.

routing.reasoning: Standard additive filter and distinct query follow existing layers, but the new audit.read-guarded endpoint and denial paths require the security override and strict test isolation.

userStories.title: Web audit query model and useAuditLog
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Create the pure audit URL/API query model and the single web API composable used by the audit page.

**Motivation** — P2 features 1–7 now record audit entries for every REST route, tool and fleet system writer, but the only way to read them is `GET /api/audit` with raw ids.

**Approach** — `lib/audit-log.ts` (pure, no Vue):

```ts
export type AuditActorType = 'USER' | 'AGENT' | 'RUNNER' | 'SYSTEM'
export interface AuditFilters {
  key: string; actorType: AuditActorType | ''; actorId: string; approverId: string
  projectId: string; resourceType: string; resourceId: string; correlationId: string
  from: string; to: string   // 'YYYY-MM-DD' or ''
  page: number               // >= 1
}
export const EMPTY_AUDIT_FILTERS: AuditFilters
export const AUDIT_PAGE_SIZE = 50
export function parseAuditRoute(query: Record<string, QueryValue>): AuditFilters
export function auditRouteQuery(filters: AuditFilters): Record<string, string>
export function auditApiQuery(filters: AuditFilters): Record<string, string>
export function withFilter(filters: AuditFilters, patch: Partial<Omit<AuditFilters, 'page'>>): AuditFilters
export function relatedFilters(correlationId: string): AuditFilters
export function principalLabel(principal: { type: string; id: string }, name: string | null): string
```

- `QueryValue` (a route query value: string, null, undefined or an array of them) is defined locally in `lib/audit-log.ts`; the helpers in `lib/fleet-log-query.ts` are module-private, so `first` and `cut` are copied, not imported.
- `parseAuditRoute` reads the first string of each route value, trimmed, cut to 128 characters; an `actorType` outside the four types becomes `''`; a `from` / `to` that is not `YYYY-MM-DD` becomes `''`; `page` is a positive integer, else 1. Mirrors `lib/fleet-log-query.ts` (`first`, `cut`).
- `auditRouteQuery` emits only non-empty fields, and `page` only when it is above 1.
- `auditApiQuery` emits the non-empty filter fields plus `current` (the page) and `size` (`'50'`), all as strings. Field names are the API's (`ListAuditQuery`): `key`, `actorType`, `actorId`, `approverId`, `projectId`, `resourceType`, `resourceId`, `correlationId`, `from`, `to`.
- `withFilter` returns a new object with the patch applied and `page` reset to 1; it never mutates its input.
- `relatedFilters` returns `EMPTY_AUDIT_FILTERS` with only `correlationId` set.
- `principalLabel` returns `name` when it is a non-empty string, else the id.

`composables/useAuditLog.ts`, the only place the page touches the API (`.nax/rules/web.md` § API Access):

```ts
export interface AuditEntry { /* AuditEntryDto fields, including display */ }
export function useAuditLog(): {
  entries: Ref<AuditEntry[]>; total: Ref<number>; hasNext: Ref<boolean>; pending: Ref<boolean>
  keys: Ref<string[]>
  load(filters: AuditFilters): Promise<void>   // GET /audit with auditApiQuery(filters)
  loadKeys(): Promise<void>                    // GET /audit/keys
}
```

A failed `load` or `loadKeys` rethrows and leaves the previous state in place (`useAdminUsers` pattern).

**Scope** — In: four new files implementing/testing helpers and the composable. Export AuditEntry with every DTO field including display.actor/onBehalfOf/approver and nullable display.project { slug, name }, actor, nullable onBehalfOf, origin, approval { requiredMode, satisfiedBy, approverType, approverId, requestId }, correlationId, summary and ISO createdAt. Use $api.get('/audit', { query: auditApiQuery(filters) }) and $api.get('/audit/keys') on already-unwrapped responses. Out: API contracts (US-001/002), page controls/i18n (US-004/005/006), detail/navigation (US-007). Discarding out-of-order `GET /audit` responses when the URL changes quickly is out of scope; each load writes its result when it resolves.

**Interface** — The TypeScript declarations above are the public contracts. Use locally defined QueryValue and refs imported from Vue only in the composable; the pure library has no Vue dependency. Preserve existing files: US-003 only creates files. Tests use fake $api responses to assert exact query calls, updates on success, pending cleanup and retained snapshots on rejection; helper tests assert empty/default serialization, trimming, array values, length bounds, immutable reset and related-request filters.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] parseAuditRoute({}) returns EMPTY_AUDIT_FILTERS, whose string fields are all '' and whose page is 1.

[unit] parseAuditRoute({ key: ' ticket.create ', actorId: ['a1', 'a2'], projectId: 'p1', from: '2026-10-01', page: '3' }) returns EMPTY_AUDIT_FILTERS with key 'ticket.create', actorId 'a1', projectId 'p1', from '2026-10-01' and page 3.
[unit] parseAuditRoute({ actorType: 'BOGUS', to: 'yesterday', page: 'abc' }) returns EMPTY_AUDIT_FILTERS.
[unit] parseAuditRoute({ resourceId: <a 200-character string> }) returns a resourceId of 128 characters.
[unit] auditRouteQuery of EMPTY_AUDIT_FILTERS with key 'ticket.create' and page 2 returns { key: 'ticket.create', page: '2' }.

[unit] auditApiQuery of EMPTY_AUDIT_FILTERS with actorType 'AGENT', actorId 'a1', from '2026-10-01' and page 2 returns { actorType: 'AGENT', actorId: 'a1', from: '2026-10-01', current: '2', size: '50' }.
[unit] withFilter of filters with key 'ticket.create' and page 3, patched with { projectId: 'p1' }, returns filters with key 'ticket.create', projectId 'p1' and page 1.
[unit] relatedFilters('c-1') returns EMPTY_AUDIT_FILTERS with correlationId 'c-1'.
[unit] principalLabel({ type: 'USER', id: 'u1' }, 'Ada') returns 'Ada'.
[unit] principalLabel({ type: 'SYSTEM', id: 'scheduler' }, null) returns 'scheduler'.
[unit] When useAuditLog().load(filters) runs over a fake $api, it calls $api.get('/audit', { query: auditApiQuery(filters) }).
[unit] When useAuditLog().load(filters) resolves over a fake $api answering one entry with total 1 and hasNext true, entries holds that one entry and hasNext is true.
[unit] When useAuditLog().loadKeys() runs over a fake $api answering { keys: ['comment.create'] }, it calls $api.get('/audit/keys') and sets keys to ['comment.create'].
[unit] When a second load rejects, useAuditLog.load rethrows the error and entries keeps the entries of the first load.

routing.reasoning: Four additive files implement deterministic query helpers and a standard update-on-success composable, with no new dependencies or access-control enforcement.

userStories.title: Audit log page: list, filters and click-to-filter
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Create the default-layout Admin Audit log page with a URL-driven filter row, resolved audit table and clickable exact-match filters.

**Motivation** — The redesign doc (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-approval-redesign-design.md` §6, "P2 page") calls for an Audit log page: "Filter by actor, approver, key, project and date."

**Approach** — `pages/admin/audit.vue`, layout `default`, title and subtitle via `PageHeader`:

- **Explicit imports.** `audit.vue` imports `useAuditLog` from `~/composables/useAuditLog` and the helpers from `~/lib/audit-log` explicitly (the test harness `mountSfc` injects only its fixed `NUXT_AUTO_IMPORTS` list, which does not hold `useAuditLog`).
- **State in the URL.** The page derives its filters with `parseAuditRoute(route.query)` and loads on mount and on every route-query change. Every control writes the URL with `router.replace({ query: auditRouteQuery(next) })` and never loads directly (pattern: `pages/admin/fleet/analytics.vue`).
- **Filter row** (`FilterBar`): key select and actor type select as `FleetNativeSelect` (`components/fleet/NativeSelect.vue`, `testid` prop rendered as `data-testid`, emits `update:modelValue`; page tests register the real component as `fleet-analytics-page.spec.ts` does), date `from` and `to` inputs (the ui `Input` with `type="date"`, bound with `:model-value` and `@update:model-value`, not a native `v-model` input; labelled as UTC days), and a Refresh button. The key options are "All keys" (`''`) plus `keys`, plus the current `filters.key` when it is set and not in `keys` (so a URL key or a failed keys load never leaves the select blank). Actor type options: all (`''`), USER, AGENT, RUNNER, SYSTEM.
- **Table**, one row per entry: local time (`toLocaleString` in the active locale), key, actor (`principalLabel(actor, display.actor)` with an actor-type badge, and "on behalf of <name>" when `onBehalfOf` is set), project (`display.project.slug`, else the raw `projectId`, else a dash), resource (`resourceType` and `resourceId`), summary (interpolated text, never `v-html`).
- **Click to filter.** Clicking a row's actor applies `{ actorType, actorId }`; its project applies `{ projectId }`; its resource applies `{ resourceType, resourceId }` (all through `withFilter`).

**Test ids** the ACs rely on: `audit-row` (one per entry), `audit-actor` / `audit-project` / `audit-resource` (the clickable cells), `audit-key-filter` and `audit-actor-type-filter` (the `FleetNativeSelect` `testid`s), `audit-from`, `audit-to`. Reserve `audit-refresh`, `audit-chip`/`audit-chip-remove`, `audit-prev`/`audit-next`, `audit-admin-only`, `audit-empty`, `audit-expand`, `audit-detail` and `audit-show-related` for downstream stories. The filter row's Refresh behavior is implemented in US-006, not this story.

**Scope** — In: new page, mounted-page list/filter tests and the admin.audit title/subtitle/filter/column/actor-type/on-behalf-of keys in both en.json and zh.json, preserving all existing locale keys. Load entries and keys independently on mount through the real composable. Out: active chips (US-005), working Refresh/paging/refusal/error/empty states (US-006), expansion/detail/navigation (US-007). Live updates, polling or SSE on the audit page are out of scope; the page loads on mount, on URL change and on Refresh. Actor, approver or project picker dropdowns are out of scope; those filters are applied by clicking a row value and removed through their chip. Linking a row's resource to its own page (ticket, job, thread) is out of scope. Date filtering in the browser's time zone is out of scope: `from` / `to` are UTC days, as the API defines them. Free-text or prefix search over keys, summaries or resource ids is out of scope; the key filter is an exact match chosen from `GET /api/audit/keys`.

**Interface** — Use the US-003 public functions without reimplementing them:
```ts
export function parseAuditRoute(query: Record<string, QueryValue>): AuditFilters
export function auditRouteQuery(filters: AuditFilters): Record<string, string>
export function withFilter(filters: AuditFilters, patch: Partial<Omit<AuditFilters, 'page'>>): AuditFilters
export function principalLabel(principal: { type: string; id: string }, name: string | null): string
```

ACs mount pages/admin/audit.vue for real using tests/pages/fleet-analytics-page.spec.ts: a fake $api, reactive route whose query the replace spy overwrites, useRoute/useRouter globals, a global permission set holding audit.read, uiStubs plus a passthrough FilterBar stub and the real useAuditLog underneath. Register real FleetNativeSelect and remove its uiStubs placeholder. Assert requests made by the page, not a replacement composable's load spy. Keep raw strings in interpolation. All filter changes reset page to 1 via withFilter; query watchers, not event handlers, trigger the resulting loads.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] When pages/admin/audit.vue is mounted with an empty route query, it calls $api.get('/audit', { query: { current: '1', size: '50' } }).
[unit] When the page is mounted with an empty route query, it calls $api.get('/audit/keys').

[unit] When mounted with route query { key: 'ticket.create', actorType: 'AGENT', from: '2026-10-01' }, the page calls $api.get('/audit', ...) with query { key: 'ticket.create', actorType: 'AGENT', from: '2026-10-01', current: '1', size: '50' }.

[unit] An audit-row whose entry has onBehalfOf { type: 'USER', id: 'u2' } and display.onBehalfOf 'Bea' shows 'Bea'.
[unit] When route.query changes from {} to { projectId: 'p1' } after mount, the page calls $api.get('/audit', ...) again with query { projectId: 'p1', current: '1', size: '50' }.
[unit] When audit-key-filter emits update:modelValue with 'comment.create', the page calls router.replace with { query: { key: 'comment.create' } }.
[unit] When audit-actor-type-filter emits update:modelValue with 'RUNNER', the page calls router.replace with { query: { actorType: 'RUNNER' } }.
[unit] When audit-from is set to '2026-10-01' on route query { page: '3' }, the page calls router.replace with { query: { from: '2026-10-01' } }.
[unit] When the audit-actor cell of a row whose actor is { type: 'AGENT', id: 'a1' } is clicked, the page calls router.replace with { query: { actorType: 'AGENT', actorId: 'a1' } }.
[unit] When the audit-project cell of a row whose projectId is 'p1' is clicked, the page calls router.replace with { query: { projectId: 'p1' } }.
[unit] When the audit-resource cell of a row with resource 'ticket'/'t1' is clicked, the page calls router.replace with { query: { resourceType: 'ticket', resourceId: 't1' } }.

userStories.title: Audit log page: active-filter chips
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add removable active id-filter chips to the URL-driven audit page, showing resolved labels when a matching loaded entry exists.

**Motivation** — The redesign doc (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-approval-redesign-design.md` §6, "P2 page") calls for an Audit log page: "Filter by actor, approver, key, project and date."

**Approach** — **Active filter chips** (US-005) for the id filters (actor, approver, project, resource, correlation). An actor, approver or project chip shows the name from the first loaded entry that carries the same id (`display.*`), else the raw id; a resource chip shows `resourceType/resourceId`; a correlation chip shows the raw correlation id. Each chip and has a remove button that writes the URL without that filter (actor removes both `actorType` and `actorId`; resource removes both `resourceType` and `resourceId`).

**State in the URL.** The page derives its filters with `parseAuditRoute(route.query)` and loads on mount and on every route-query change. Every control writes the URL with `router.replace({ query: auditRouteQuery(next) })` and never loads directly (pattern: `pages/admin/fleet/analytics.vue`).

**Test ids** the ACs rely on: `audit-chip` (with `data-filter` = `actor` | `approver` | `project` | `resource` | `correlation`) and its `audit-chip-remove` button.

**Scope** — In: extend pages/admin/audit.vue created by US-004, add tests/pages/admin-audit-chips.spec.ts and additive admin.audit chip-label/remove keys to both locales, leaving existing keys unchanged. Match actor, approval.approverId or projectId to loaded records; missing data must leave a useful raw-id chip. Remove only that chip's filter(s), preserve unrelated filters and reset page to 1 via withFilter. Out: initial page/table/composable (US-003/004), paging/refresh/error/forbidden/empty behavior (US-006), expansion/detail/navigation (US-007). Actor, approver or project picker dropdowns are out of scope; those filters are applied by clicking a row value and removed through their chip.

**Interface** — Reuse the upstream helper signatures:
```ts
export function withFilter(filters: AuditFilters, patch: Partial<Omit<AuditFilters, 'page'>>): AuditFilters
export function auditRouteQuery(filters: AuditFilters): Record<string, string>
```

ACs mount pages/admin/audit.vue with the same real-composable/reactive-route harness as US-004. Find each chip by data-filter and trigger its own audit-chip-remove button; assert router.replace output, not internal helper calls. Resolve chip text only from the loaded audit display block; do not call user/agent/runner/project lists or add permission requirements.

userStories.title: Audit log page: paging, refresh and states
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Finish audit browsing with URL-held pagination, explicit refresh and independent forbidden, error and empty states.

**Motivation** — P2 features 1–7 now record audit entries for every REST route, tool and fleet system writer, but the only way to read them is `GET /api/audit` with raw ids.

**Approach** — **Paging.** Previous and Next buttons (US-006); Next is disabled when `hasNext` is false, Previous on page 1. They write `page` into the URL.

**States.** A 403 (envelope code 40003 or 403; reuse the existing `isForbidden` helper pattern of `pages/admin/roles.vue`) shows the page's admin-only message and no table. An empty page shows an empty-state message.

**State in the URL.** The page derives its filters with `parseAuditRoute(route.query)` and loads on mount and on every route-query change. Every control writes the URL with `router.replace({ query: auditRouteQuery(next) })` and never loads directly (pattern: `pages/admin/fleet/analytics.vue`). Refresh is the explicit exception: it reloads the current parsed filters without changing the URL.

Failure handling:
- `GET /audit` refused with 403: Page shows its admin-only message, no table.
- `GET /audit` refused otherwise (for example the 400 reversed window): `toast.error(extractApiError(err))`; the table keeps its last loaded rows.
- `GET /audit/keys` fails: `toast.error(extractApiError(err))`; the entry table still renders.

**Test ids** the ACs rely on: `audit-refresh`, `audit-prev`, `audit-next`, `audit-admin-only`, `audit-empty`, and the existing `audit-row`.

**Scope** — In: extend pages/admin/audit.vue after chips, add tests/pages/admin-audit-states.spec.ts and additive admin.audit paging/refresh/admin-only/empty keys to both locale JSON files, leaving existing keys unchanged. Keep query filters when paging; default page 1 is omitted in the URL. Catch both entry and keys failures without coupling their outcomes. The composable's previous rows remain visible after non-forbidden errors; forbidden view hides the table even if a prior load succeeded. Out: API date/filter validation (US-002), query/composable implementation (US-003), base list/filter controls (US-004), chips (US-005), detail/navigation (US-007). Live updates, polling or SSE on the audit page are out of scope; the page loads on mount, on URL change and on Refresh. Discarding out-of-order `GET /audit` responses when the URL changes quickly is out of scope; each load writes its result when it resolves.

**Interface** — Reuse the public composable and helpers:
```ts
load(filters: AuditFilters): Promise<void>
loadKeys(): Promise<void>
export function auditRouteQuery(filters: AuditFilters): Record<string, string>
```

Copy the local forbidden predicate behavior from roles.vue: `err instanceof ApiError && (err.code === 40003 || err.code === 403)`. API failures are presented using extractApiError, never raw err.message. Mount the same real page/composable harness as US-004. Test initial empty versus retained non-empty snapshots, second-request failures, key-load failure independent of entries, exact replace calls and same-query Refresh requests. Security-sensitive refusal rendering uses strict three-session TDD even though server authorization is already provided by the API.

[unit] When mounted on page 1, the audit-prev button is disabled.
[unit] Given GET /audit answers hasNext false, the audit-next button is disabled.
[unit] When mounted with route query { page: '2', key: 'ticket.create' }, clicking audit-prev calls router.replace with { query: { key: 'ticket.create' } }.
[unit] When audit-refresh is clicked, the page calls $api.get('/audit', ...) again with the same query as the mount load.
[unit] When GET /audit rejects with an ApiError whose code is 40003, the page renders audit-admin-only instead of the table.
[unit] When GET /audit rejects with a 400 ApiError after a first successful load, the page calls toast.error(extractApiError(err)).
[unit] When GET /audit rejects with a 400 ApiError after a first successful load, the page still renders the audit-rows of the first load.
[unit] When GET /audit/keys rejects, the page calls toast.error(extractApiError(err)).
[unit] Given GET /audit answers no entries, the page renders audit-empty and no audit-row.

routing.reasoning: Existing URL and composable patterns make paging/refresh standard, but permission-refusal handling and hiding retained data on 403 trigger strict security TDD.

userStories.title: Audit row detail and navigation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add expandable audit provenance/approval detail, Show related correlation navigation, and audit.read-gated sidebar and command-palette destinations.

**Motivation** — The redesign doc (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-approval-redesign-design.md` §6, "P2 page") calls for an Audit log page: "Filter by actor, approver, key, project and date."

**Approach** — **Row detail** (US-007): an expand control on each row shows `components/audit/AuditEntryDetail.vue`, which `audit.vue` imports explicitly (`import AuditEntryDetail from '~/components/audit/AuditEntryDetail.vue'`, as `roles.vue` imports `RoleEditorDialog`). Prop `entry: AuditEntry` (the type exported by `useAuditLog.ts`). It shows: origin label, correlation id with a "Show related" button that emits `related` with the correlation id (the page then writes `auditRouteQuery(relatedFilters(correlationId))`), approval `requiredMode` and `satisfiedBy` labels, approver (`principalLabel` over `approval.approverType` / `approverId` and `display.approver`) when present, approval request id when present, `onBehalfOf` principal when present, and the full ISO `createdAt`. The no-approval case in AC-3 is an explicit exception to showing a present request id: when `approval.satisfiedBy` is `none` and the approver is null, show neither approver nor request id. Use the DTO's nested `approval.approverType`, `approval.approverId` and `approval.requestId` fields, not invented top-level fields.

**Navigation** (US-007): `layouts/default.vue` gains a `/admin/audit` link in the Admin section, gated on `audit.read` and included in `showAdminNav`; `components/CommandPalette.vue` gains an `audit` command to `/admin/audit` when the global set holds `audit.read`.

**i18n**: `nav.audit` and the `admin.audit.*` keys in both `i18n/locales/en.json` and `zh.json`, including labels for the four actor types, the five origins (`rest`, `mcp`, `thread`, `runner`, `system`) and the four `satisfiedBy` values (`none`, `self`, `agent`, `human`).

**Test ids** the ACs rely on: `audit-expand`, `audit-detail`, `audit-show-related`. The expanded detail must be the real imported component, and its related event must reach the page's router.replace.

**Scope** — In: new AuditEntryDetail component and component tests, row expansion in pages/admin/audit.vue, related-event URL wiring, default layout link/flag/showAdminNav term, palette command and tests, nav/detail locale additions. RequiredMode labels also cover the approval mode values. Add audit.read to tests/helpers/permission-nav.ts ADMIN_NAV_KEYS and canReadAudit to adminNavFlags; add ['/admin/audit', 'audit.read'] to tests/layouts/default-permission-nav.spec.ts ADMIN_LINKS so existing per-key/no-key loops cover it. Existing assertions, links and locale keys are unchanged. Out: base query/composable/page/chips/paging states (US-003 through US-006). Filtering by origin or by on-behalf-of principal is out of scope. Linking a row's resource to its own page (ticket, job, thread) is out of scope. A project-scoped audit page or project-admin access to audit entries is out of scope: `audit.read` stays a global key. Updating `docs/ux/redesign/MASTER-PLAN.md` is out of scope (this page is not a redesign slice), subject to higher-priority repository guidance recorded in analysis.

**Interface** — Use these exact signatures/import and target flag:
```ts
import AuditEntryDetail from '~/components/audit/AuditEntryDetail.vue'
// AuditEntryDetail prop:
entry: AuditEntry
// AuditEntryDetail event:
(e: 'related', correlationId: string): void
export function relatedFilters(correlationId: string): AuditFilters
export function auditRouteQuery(filters: AuditFilters): Record<string, string>
export function principalLabel(principal: { type: string; id: string }, name: string | null): string
const canReadAudit = computed(() => globalPermissions.value.has('audit.read'))
```

Gate using useGlobalPermissions().permissions.has('audit.read'), never any role name or a project permission set. A gate hides a control, while the API remains authoritative and refusals stay surfaced through the page's existing handling. Keep inline sidebar links and source order pinned by layout tests. Mirror command-palette-roles.spec.ts for the real palette mount/navigate behavior and its native-v-model scratch workaround. Component tests assert localized origin/approval labels, null-field omission, raw fallback principals, ISO timestamp and emitted correlation id; mounted page tests assert expansion and replacement of all previous filters/page by relatedFilters.

analysis:
This is an additive enhancement to an existing permission/audit subsystem, not a greenfield implementation. Navigation used direct repository reads and text searches because codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this session; no index freshness claims are made. The actual application architecture is NestJS/Fastify plus Prisma in apps/api and Nuxt 4/Vue SSR in apps/web, not the automatically detected Express/Next.js labels: apps/api/src/audit/audit.controller.ts:1 imports Nest controllers, apps/web/pages/admin/roles.vue:1 uses Vue script setup, and .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:26 and .nax/mono/apps/web/context.md:21 document the stacks. Bun/Turborepo scripts and Node requirements are at package.json:6-24 and package.json:39-42. Read the app context and nathapp-nestjs-patterns skill before implementing Nest code; use Nathapp repository/service/controller, JsonResponse, pagination and exception conventions. No production source changes or tests were run during PRD drafting.

Existing API flow and impact: apps/api/src/audit/audit.controller.ts:12-26 implements GET /api/audit via RequiresGuard and @Requires('audit.read'), parseQuery(ListAuditQuery, rawQuery), AuditLogService.list and JsonResponse.Ok(toPageResult(...)). Its @ApiResponse deliberately has no type. apps/api/src/audit/audit-log.service.ts:10-20 defines the current query without correlationId; :24-30 expands date-only boundaries to UTC, :36-40 rejects reversed windows with audit.auditQuery, and :41-53 forwards seven non-date filters then directly passes AuditEntryDto.from to remapPage. Preserve all these existing behaviors while adding names and correlation. apps/api/src/audit/prisma-audit-entry.repository.ts:10-28 is the existing AbstractPrismaRepository and append-only mapping; :30-46 constructs exact-match predicates and uses Paginate with createdAt desc/id desc. US-001 must leave findPage unchanged; US-002 adds correlationId there. apps/api/src/audit/domain/audit-entry.domain.ts:8-39 holds flat record/filter types; :16-23 show that on-behalf-of and approver kinds are USER/AGENT whereas actor also includes RUNNER/SYSTEM. apps/api/src/audit/dto/audit-entry.dto.ts:4-46 maps records into nested actor, onBehalfOf and approval blocks, renames approvalRequestId to approval.requestId and serializes createdAt to ISO. Add display without changing any existing field. EMPTY_AUDIT_DISPLAY default preserves direct callers; passing the newly two-argument static mapper directly into remapPage is unsafe because apps/api/src/common/dto/koda-page.query.ts:75-77 uses Array.map and would supply the index as display. Use a closure. Pagination metadata is normalized by toPageResult at :69-71; retain total/current/size/hasNext/hasPrev exactly.

US-001 data projection: collect distinct USER, AGENT and RUNNER ids across actor, onBehalfOf and approver plus projectIds, call findDisplayNames once only when at least one list is non-empty, and map names by kind, not just id. Never look up SYSTEM actor ids. Select only id/name/email for users, id/name for agents/runners, id/slug/name for projects. Whitespace-only or null user names fall back to email; missing rows return null display fields; do not filter deletedAt on historical projects. A DB lookup error rejects the page, not a partially enriched success. This is the spec's explicit narrow exception to cross-module service reads: .nax/rules/api-data.md:26-65 ordinarily requires owning-module services, but a global audit module must not import four domain modules merely to project labels. apps/api/src/audit/audit-log.module.ts:10-23 is already global, registers the repository internally, and exports AuditRecorder and AuditLogService only. Keep that wiring and the repository token private. Text search found DTO consumers only in the audit service/tests and repository consumers in the audit storage, module and service; no existing web audit consumer needs migration. Do not change write-side attribution, recorder/storage behavior or audit immutability.

US-002 API contract: add correlationId through ListAuditQuery, AuditListQuery, AuditEntryFilters, list and findPage. Follow the neighboring @ApiPropertyOptional/@IsOptional/@IsString/@MaxLength(128) fields in apps/api/src/audit/dto/list-audit.query.ts:11-27; dates at :29-35 remain UTC-only. Add GET /api/audit/keys to the same controller with the same guard/key, return JsonResponse.Ok({ keys }), and delegate through service.keys to repository.findDistinctKeys. The distinct query is select-only, sorted ascending, and deliberately unpaged because the key set is bounded in practice; do not derive it from the permission catalog. Existing schema apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:831-859 already stores all required data and has no principal/project foreign keys. Its indexes cover key, actor, project, approver and resource but not correlationId; the new correlation predicate may scan as history grows. No schema/data migration is specified; do not silently broaden this feature into retention or indexing work. Regenerate root openapi.json only after US-001 and US-002 contracts exist, using bun run api:export-spec (package.json:20), not bun run generate, which also regenerates the excluded CLI client. Only operation/query additions are required, no AuditEntryDto/AuditKeysDto component schemas. Keep workdir apps/api as binding even though this story intentionally updates root openapi.json.

API test seams: apps/api/src/audit/audit-log.service.spec.ts:20-24 currently mocks only findPage; it must gain a findDisplayNames empty-maps mock so the unchanged AC-1..AC-7 assertions remain meaningful (:27-66). Its AC-7 compares AuditEntryDto.from(record), so the default null block preserves compatibility. apps/api/src/audit/dto/audit-entry.dto.spec.ts:12-31 pins actor/onBehalfOf/approval/ISO serialization; preserve existing AC-8..AC-13 and add default display coverage. New repository unit tests use fake Prisma delegates to prove select-only bounded-by-page lookup behavior without a DB. Real route behavior belongs in the two new integration files, mirroring apps/api/test/integration/audit/audit-route.integration.spec.ts:15-46 (canRunDbTests, bootHttpApp, seedFleetHttpWorld, fixtureDb, role fixtures, per-test audit cleanup, app shutdown). Direct fixture audit inserts avoid recording unintended writes in distinct-key assertions. Reuse seeded users and set names via db.user.update; agents use seedFleetHttpAgent and runners use insertRunner. Existing route tests at :48-102 cover newest ordering, UTC inclusive dates, exact filters, project-admin/global-agent denial, unauthenticated 401 and reversed-window 400. Endpoint registration coverage must extend apps/api/test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts:342-348 and apps/api/test/integration/openapi-spec/spec-integrity.integration.spec.ts:18 without weakening existing checks. Vitest uses vi, not jest. DB runs require KODA_DB_TESTS=1 outside NAX_SANDBOXED=1; skips are not verification. Tests reset the DB, so do not run DB suites concurrently against the same database; use a private test container for a second checkout. Module/DI tests remain DB-free co-located unit tests.

US-003 browser foundation: apps/web/lib/fleet-log-query.ts:26-39 has module-private QueryValue/first/cut helpers, including surrogate-safe truncation; copy the helpers locally rather than exporting or importing them. first currently reads the array's first element if it is a string, matching the existing pattern. Parse route values leniently into explicit empty strings, allow only four actor types, accept browser date fields only as YYYY-MM-DD, normalize positive integer pages, and cap filter strings at 128. URL query uses page only above 1; API query always sends current and size=50. withFilter resets page immutably; relatedFilters discards all previous filters. apps/web/composables/useAdminUsers.ts:28-51 is the state/update-on-success/finally pending pattern: useAuditLog should update entries/total/hasNext only after GET succeeds and keep the prior snapshot on a rejection; loadKeys independently preserves its previous keys on error. apps/web/composables/useApi.ts:1-96 defines JsonResponse unwrapping, ApiError and extractApiError; :163-285 handles SSR internal base, cookie-forwarding request fetch, locale headers, retries and relative $api methods. The audit composable must use relative /audit and /audit/keys and consume already-unwrapped payloads, not raw envelopes or direct fetch. Export a complete AuditEntry mirror including nested nullable display, approval and onBehalfOf types; never import API runtime code into web.

US-004 through US-006 page architecture: create pages/admin/audit.vue with default layout and PageHeader. Explicitly import useAuditLog and pure helpers. Filters derive from reactive route.query and every filter/pagination action router.replace's auditRouteQuery; only mount, a query watcher and Refresh initiate loads. The URL pattern is visible in apps/web/pages/admin/fleet/analytics.vue:94-100 and :137-143, but do not copy its useRefetchOnVisible polling/backstop hook. FilterBar's slot/grid API is apps/web/components/FilterBar.vue:8-18. FleetNativeSelect actually maps testid to data-testid and emits update:modelValue (apps/web/components/fleet/NativeSelect.vue:1-38); use the real component in tests, not uiStubs' placeholder. Date Input controls use :model-value/@update:model-value and explicit UTC-day labels, not native v-model. Always include a URL-selected key missing from fetched keys. Table uses locale-aware local timestamps, actor type badges, resolved labels with raw id fallbacks, project slug or id or dash, resource type/id and interpolated summary. Id chips read the first matching entry's display label, otherwise raw ids; removal clears paired actor/resource fields together and resets page. Keep raw audit strings escaped through Vue interpolation. US-006 adds paging and refresh; 403 is a distinct no-table state, empty is distinct from a failed refresh, and non-403 errors toast while keeping prior rows. Keys failure must never suppress a successful entries response. apps/web/pages/admin/roles.vue:22-38 and apps/web/pages/admin/users.vue:36-40 demonstrate that ApiError.code is envelope ret 40003, not necessarily HTTP 403. Recognize both 40003 and 403. No stale-response generation mechanism is needed: out-of-order response handling is explicitly deferred.

Web test integration: apps/web/tests/pages/fleet-analytics-page.spec.ts:101-153 demonstrates reactive route.query, a replace spy that mutates it, real API composables and settle loops. Reuse this style for the three new audit page suites, with a fake $api and a global permission set containing audit.read. apps/web/tests/helpers/mount-sfc.ts:122-147 lists fixed Nuxt auto-imports and does not contain useAuditLog, hence the mandatory explicit import; do not expand the harness just to hide that seam. The harness already registers FleetNativeSelect at :277 and :292. Supply a passthrough FilterBar stub so controls render. Use the real useAuditLog beneath mounted page tests to verify the US-002/003/004 seam, not a load spy replacing the whole composable. Keep all specified data-testid contracts stable.

US-007 detail and navigation: create AuditEntryDetail.vue with entry: AuditEntry and a related event, explicitly import it in the page, and wire expanded-row events into router.replace(auditRouteQuery(relatedFilters(id))). ApprovalMode/satisfiedBy are defined by apps/api/src/action-context/action-context.ts:34-45; use localized requiredMode and satisfiedBy labels including none/self/agent/human, and localized rest/mcp/thread/runner/system origins. Show full ISO time in detail, local time in the table. outOfScope: Exporting audit entries (CSV, JSON download) is out of scope.
A project-scoped audit page or project-admin access to audit entries is out of scope: `audit.read` stays a global key.
Live updates, polling or SSE on the audit page are out of scope; the page loads on mount, on URL change and on Refresh.
A CLI `koda audit` command and regenerating `apps/cli/src/generated/` are out of scope.
Free-text or prefix search over keys, summaries or resource ids is out of scope; the key filter is an exact match chosen from `GET /api/audit/keys`.
Filtering by origin or by on-behalf-of principal is out of scope.
Actor, approver or project picker dropdowns are out of scope; those filters are applied by clicking a row value and removed through their chip.
Linking a row's resource to its own page (ticket, job, thread) is out of scope.
Date filtering in the browser's time zone is out of scope: `from` / `to` are UTC days, as the API defines them.
Retention, deletion or redaction of audit entries is out of scope.
An `AuditEntryDto` or `AuditKeysDto` component schema in `openapi.json` is out of scope (the routes' `@ApiResponse` carries no `type`, as on `AuditController.list`).
Updating `docs/ux/redesign/MASTER-PLAN.md` is out of scope (this page is not a redesign slice).
Discarding out-of-order `GET /audit` responses when the URL changes quickly is out of scope; each load writes its result when it resolves.
Auditing the remaining writers, assistant tools and the coverage guard are out of scope (next feature, `permissions-p2-audit-integrations`).
